title: Contexts and Signals
text: Decimal operations signal noteworthy conditions: result rounded, division hit zero, value overflowed. happens next depends context, signal gets one three dispositions: Trapped — operation raises classed R error. Reported — signal recorded flag surfaced warning. default signal haven’t trapped. Silent — signal recorded flag . flags sticky: raised, stay raised clear , can run whole computation check afterwards happened along way: operations round fit two significant digits, raising inexact rounded; flags simply stay raised across whole block. Use clear_decimal_flags() start fresh slate computation want audit.
code: ctx <- decimal_context(precision = 2L, traps = character()) with_decimal_context(ctx, {   clear_decimal_flags()   decimal("1.25") + decimal("0")   decimal("1") / decimal("8")   decimal_flags() }) #> [1] "inexact" "rounded"

title: Decimal Values
text: Arithmetic vectorized, context-controlled, keeps track significance: One difference base R worth knowing : %% %/%. Base R floors integer division toward negative infinity, General Decimal Arithmetic truncates toward zero, results differ negative operands:
code: decimal("1.20") + decimal("2.3") #> <decimal[1]> #> [1] 3.50 sum(decimal(c("1.20", "2.30", "3.40"))) #> <decimal[1]> #> [1] 6.90 mean(decimal(c("1", "2", "3"))) #> <decimal[1]> #> [1] 2 -7 %% 4                        # base R: floored, remainder takes divisor's sign #> [1] 1 decimal("-7") %% decimal("4")  # decimal: truncated, remainder takes dividend's sign #> <decimal[1]> #> [1] -3  -7 %/% 4 #> [1] -2 decimal("-7") %/% decimal("4") #> <decimal[1]> #> [1] -1

title: Decimal Values
text: decimal supports full menagerie: NA, NaNs, infinities, signed zero — keeps R’s missing value distinct decimal’s --number: things note: NA R missing value — ’s absent computation entirely. NaN (quiet NaN) sNaN (signaling NaN) decimal --number values participate arithmetic. quiet NaN propagates silently; sNaN raises invalid_operation signal, error default context — see vignette("contexts--signals"). .na() returns TRUE NA decimal NaNs, matching base R’s .na(NaN). Use .nan() tell decimal NaN apart missing value. Signed zero survives formatting: -0 prints -0, 0.
code: x <- decimal(c(NA_character_, "NaN", "sNaN", "Infinity", "-0")) x #> <decimal[5]> #> [1] <NA>     NaN      sNaN     Infinity -0 is.na(x) #> [1]  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE FALSE is.nan(x) #> [1] FALSE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE FALSE number_class(x) #> [1] NA          "NaN"       "sNaN"      "+Infinity" "-Zero"

text: quantize() workhorse rounding: rescales x scale declared quantum, using active context’s rounding mode. ’s operation behind round() signif(), reads naturally common case — rounding cents: normalize() strips shared trailing zeros finest scale vector actually needs, without discarding element’s significance: fma(, b, c) computes * b + c one fused operation single rounding end, instead rounding multiplication addition: same_quantum() reports whether two vectors share declared scale (remember, scale per-vector property): adjusted() returns value’s adjusted exponent — exponent scientific notation single digit point:
code: quantize(decimal("1.2345"), decimal("0.01")) #> <decimal[1]> #> [1] 1.23 normalize(decimal(c("1.2300", "1.2"))) #> <decimal[2]> #> [1] 1.23 1.20 fma(decimal("2"), decimal("3"), decimal("4")) #> <decimal[1]> #> [1] 10 same_quantum(decimal(c("1.20", "2.0")), decimal(c("2.30", "3.00"))) #> [1] TRUE TRUE adjusted(decimal(c("1.2300", "1E-3"))) #> [1]  0 -3

title: Exact Arbitrary-Precision Decimal Vectors
text: decimal provides exact, arbitrary-precision decimal vectors R. ’ve ever surprised 0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3 FALSE, package : Doubles binary fractions, can’t represent decimal numbers exactly, tiny errors accumulate compute. ’s usually fine — ’re working money, invoices, exchange rates, anything else cents add . decimal uses decimal representation performs arithmetic explicit decimal context, rounding controlled observable. hood, decimal built : mpdecimal, battle-tested C library behind Python’s decimal module, implementing General Decimal Arithmetic standard. vctrs, decimal vectors work naturally data frames, tibbles, dplyr::mutate(), joins, sorting, everything else already vectors. Highlights: Exact values. Strings integers parsed exactly; promotion finer shared scale adds trailing zeros. Values round-trip .character() without loss — nothing changes way CSV file database column back. Full arithmetic. +, -, *, /, ^, %%, %/%, comparisons, math functions like abs(), sqrt(), exp(), log(), plus reductions sum(), prod(), min(), max(), mean(). Decimal-aware tools. quantize() round fixed number digits (say, cents), normalize(), fma(), same_quantum(), adjusted(), number_class(). control rules. decimal context sets precision, rounding mode, conditions (overflow, division zero, …) errors — see vignette("contexts--signals"). Special values. NA, signed zeros, infinities, quiet signaling NaNs supported throughout.
code: library(decimal)  0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3 #> [1] FALSE decimal("0.1") + decimal("0.2") == decimal("0.3") #> [1] TRUE

title: Exact Arbitrary-Precision Decimal Vectors
text: Create decimal vectors strings (exact, recommended way) integers, use like numeric vector: Decimal vectors first-class citizens tibbles dplyr pipelines: Exactness matters small errors compound — literally, case interest:
code: library(decimal)  x <- decimal(c("1.20", "2.30", "3.40")) x #> <decimal[3]> #> [1] 1.20 2.30 3.40  sum(x) #> <decimal[1]> #> [1] 6.90 mean(x) #> <decimal[1]> #> [1] 2.30 library(dplyr)  sales <- tibble::tibble(   item  = c("coffee", "bagel", "juice"),   price = decimal(c("2.50", "1.25", "3.95")),   qty   = c(3L, 2L, 1L) )  sales |>   mutate(total = price * qty) |>   summarise(revenue = sum(total)) #> # A tibble: 1 × 1 #>   revenue #>     <dec> #> 1   13.95 principal <- decimal(c("1000.00", "2500.00", "500.00")) rate <- decimal("0.05")  balance <- principal * (1L + rate)^4L balance #> <decimal[3]> #> [1] 1215.5062500000 3038.7656250000 607.7531250000  # round to cents for reporting quantize(balance, decimal("0.01")) #> <decimal[3]> #> [1] 1215.51 3038.77 607.75
